plain: Getting money from someone by force or threats.

webster.text: The act of extorting; the act or practice of wresting any thing from a person by force, duress, menaces, authority, or by any undue exercise of power; illegal exaction; illegal compulsion to pay money, or to do some other act.

more.text: Force or illegal compulsion by which any thing is taken from a person.

example.quote: a repeated succession of laws has been made to suppress their iniquitous speculations and cruel extortions;
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 5, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
